name: Open blue carbon registry
summary: An open, public registry of blue carbon ecosystems (mangroves, seagrass meadows and salt marshes): where they are, who keeps them, what is measured there, and what has been promised and paid. Every claim carries its sources and settles only when independent lines of evidence agree. Version 0 is live with its first site, Mikoko Pamoja in Kenya, and reads credit records from national registries through the CAD Trust network. It records; it does not issue or sell credits.
input_wanted: Sites, with the communities who keep them
Open maps and datasets for mangrove, seagrass and salt-marsh extent
Measurement methods for carbon stocks and their uncertainty
National registries ready to connect through CAD Trust

name: Whale sanctuary community
summary: A community on Cloud Mirror for tohorā, the whales, as legal persons, following He Whakaputanga Moana, the 2024 Declaration for the Ocean signed by Māori and Pacific Indigenous leaders. Being designed in conversation with Mere Takoko of the Pacific Whale Fund and the Moananui Sanctuary Trust. Indigenous partners shape its charter, and its rules are written so other places can adopt them.
input_wanted: Indigenous governance and guardianship: who speaks for the whales
Protections for traditional knowledge and Indigenous data
Sighting, acoustic and ship-strike data as independent evidence
Sanctuary areas to map against marine protected areas and blue carbon

name: Indigenous and community lands layer
summary: Proposed with the Tropical Forest Forever Facility at COP31: a data layer on Gaia showing Indigenous and community lands next to forests, blue carbon sites, marine protected areas and the payments meant to reach them, including the at least 20% of Tropical Forest Forever Facility payments committed to Indigenous Peoples and local communities. It links to existing maps such as LandMark rather than copying them, publishes nothing without the free, prior and informed consent of the people concerned, and keeps the data under their control. The people of each territory would hold first claim to any value from it, such as Ven Oxygen or DIRT, and overlapping claims are shown openly so they can be resolved or governed together. Rewards follow the evidence: satellite data over each territory, checked against the community's own monitoring.
input_wanted: Indigenous partners to govern the layer and shape its rules
What should never appear on a public map
Territories, ideally in Tropical Forest Forever Facility countries, whose people want to pilot it
Reporting on where Indigenous and community payments actually go

name: Chocó Pacific guardians
summary: A community on Cloud Mirror for the Afro-descendant and Indigenous communities of Colombia's Chocó Pacific coast, one of the most biodiverse marine corridors on Earth. Started at the COP31 Climate Campus leadership dinner. It puts their vital needs first (water, energy and connectivity), then education and tourism, and builds self-sustaining economic models that pay communities for the conservation they already lead as guardians of the coast: mangroves in the open blue carbon registry, ocean monitoring for the Ocean Data Initiative, and first claim on any value from their territory. The communities govern it, and nothing is published without their consent.
input_wanted: Community councils and Indigenous authorities to govern it and choose a pilot
The most urgent vital need (water, energy or connectivity) and partners to fund it
Monitoring communities already do on mangroves, fisheries and marine protected areas
What should never appear on a public map

name: Ocean Data Initiative
summary: Open ocean data, refreshed every week: tide gauges, buoys and Argo floats checked against ocean models, coral reef heat stress, and marine protection and ocean finance for every Atlantic Rim country, as map layers any GIS tool can read.
input_wanted: New open sources and partner datasets
Corrections where a measurement and a model disagree

name: The commons registry
summary: A registry of commons, each placed on the rules ladder (no rules, weak rules, no payout) with its boundaries, users, rules and remuneration, and every claim backed by evidence from independent sources.
input_wanted: Commons to add, with the people who use them
Better evidence for, or against, a claim already listed

name: Library of the Commons
summary: A map of Elinor Ostrom's academic lineage, starting with the 149 Workshop PhDs and affiliated scholars, as the start of a brain trust that can answer place-specific questions about governing a commons.
input_wanted: Scholars missing from the first generation
Later affiliations, current work and key publications
The second generation: students of these scholars

name: Marine protected area pilot
summary: One marine protected area, governed with the people who fish and dive there: clear boundaries, local rules, monitoring that pairs community testimony with independent measurement, and payouts to its keepers.
input_wanted: A candidate MPA with an active local group
Monitoring data and partners on the ground

name: Medicine from biodiversity
summary: Turning the voluntary global benefit-sharing rule for genetic sequence data into payouts that reach the places and peoples the data comes from.
input_wanted: Cases of medicines traced to a specific place or people
Companies willing to contribute and report

name: AI agent commons
summary: Rules for the shared networks where AI agents meet: identity, an accountable owner, a charter they accept, verification that counts agents of one model as one voice, and a levy that funds the commons.
input_wanted: Agent builders willing to join under a charter
Views on fees, findings and appeals for agents
